tools.name: get_seo_meta
tools.description: Read the Rank Math SEO fields (meta title, meta description, focus keyword, canonical, robots) of one post or page on a connected WordPress site. Identify the item by post_id or by slug.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_id.description: Numeric id of the post or page. Give this OR slug.
post_id.title: Post Id

slug.description: Slug of the post or page, e.g. 'about-us'. Used when post_id is not given.
slug.title: Slug

post_type.description: Optional post type ('post', 'page', or a custom type) to disambiguate a slug used by several items.
post_type.title: Post Type

return_schema.description:
Rank Math SEO fields for a single post or page.

Empty strings mean "no SEO value set" — Rank Math then falls back to its
own template for that post type, so an empty meta_title is normal, not a
failure. robots is a list because Rank Math stores it as an array.
return_schema.title: SeoMeta

tools.name: update_seo_meta
tools.description: Update the Rank Math SEO fields of one post or page on a connected WordPress site: meta title, meta description, and optionally focus keyword, canonical URL and robots directives. Identify the item by post_id or by slug. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_id.description: Numeric id of the post or page. Give this OR slug.
post_id.title: Post Id

slug.description: Slug of the post or page, e.g. 'about-us'. Used when post_id is not given.
slug.title: Slug

post_type.description: Optional post type ('post', 'page', or a custom type) to disambiguate a slug used by several items.
post_type.title: Post Type

meta_title.description: New Rank Math SEO title. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.
meta_title.title: Meta Title

meta_description.description: New Rank Math meta description. Omit to leave unchanged; pass an empty string to clear it.
meta_description.title: Meta Description

canonical_url.description: Optional canonical URL. Omit to leave unchanged; empty string clears it.
canonical_url.title: Canonical Url

robots.description: Optional robots directives, e.g. ['noindex','nofollow']. Allowed: index, noindex, nofollow, noarchive, noimageindex, nosnippet. Omit to leave unchanged.
robots.title: Robots

focus_keyword.description: Optional Rank Math focus keyword. Omit to leave unchanged.
focus_keyword.title: Focus Keyword

return_schema.description:
Rank Math SEO fields for a single post or page.

Empty strings mean "no SEO value set" — Rank Math then falls back to its
own template for that post type, so an empty meta_title is normal, not a
failure. robots is a list because Rank Math stores it as an array.
return_schema.title: SeoMeta

tools.name: get_builder_content
tools.description: Read the Elementor and/or Bricks page-builder element tree of one post or page on a connected WordPress site, flattened into a simple list of elements with ids, types, and settings. Identify the item by post_id or by slug. Each result row carries a state_token required to edit any of its elements.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_id.description: Numeric id of the post or page. Give this OR slug.
post_id.title: Post Id

slug.description: Slug of the post or page, e.g. 'home'. Used when post_id is not given.
slug.title: Slug

post_type.description: Optional post type ('post', 'page', or a custom type) to disambiguate a slug used by several items.
post_type.title: Post Type

builder.description: Optional: 'elementor' or 'bricks', to read only that builder when both are active on the item.
builder.title: Builder

BuilderContent.description:
One builder's (or one Bricks zone's) element tree for a single post.

state_token is required to call update_builder_field against any element
in this exact tree — copy it from here, do not invent it.
BuilderContent.title: BuilderContent

BuilderElement.description:
One flattened builder element row: a widget, section, column or container.

Nesting is expressed by parent_id (this row's parent element_id), not by
physical structure — both Elementor's tree and Bricks' flat array are
flattened into this same shape so a caller doesn't need two mental models.
BuilderElement.title: BuilderElement

tools.name: update_builder_field
tools.description: Change exactly ONE settings field on exactly ONE existing Elementor or Bricks element, identified by element_id from a previous get_builder_content call. Requires the exact state_token from that same read; the write is refused if the page changed since. Cannot create elements or replace the page — point edits only.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_id.description: Numeric id of the post or page. Give this OR slug.
post_id.title: Post Id

slug.description: Slug of the post or page. Used when post_id is not given.
slug.title: Slug

post_type.description: Optional post type to disambiguate a slug used by several items.
post_type.title: Post Type

element_id.description: Builder-native id of the exact element to edit — from a previous get_builder_content call
element_id.title: Element Id

field.description: Name of the single settings field to change on that element, e.g. 'title' or '_typography'
field.title: Field

value.description: New value for the field — a plain string/number for simple fields, or an object for structured ones like {'unit': 'px', 'size': 20}
value.title: Value

state_token.description: Exact state_token from a previous get_builder_content call for this item/builder/zone — the write is refused if the page changed since
state_token.title: State Token

builder.description: 'elementor' or 'bricks' — required only when both are active on the same item
builder.title: Builder

zone.description: Bricks only: 'header', 'content', or 'footer' — which template area the element lives in
zone.title: Zone

tools.name: check_builder_support
tools.description: Check whether a connected WordPress site can read/edit Elementor or Bricks page-builder content — whether the Imperal Builder Bridge plugin is installed and which builder plugin(s) are active site-wide.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

tools.name: scan_builder_content
tools.description: Diagnostic scan of a connected WordPress site's database for ANY post, page, or template (including custom post types like bricks_template that list_pages/list_posts never see, since they are not registered for the normal REST posts endpoints) carrying non-empty Elementor or Bricks builder content. Use this when get_builder_content reports BUILDER_NONE_ACTIVE on the items you tried, to find where builder content actually lives on the site. Read-only; requires Builder Bridge plugin v1.1.0 or later.

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

BuilderScanItem.description:
One post/page/template found by the /builder/scan diagnostic to carry
non-empty Elementor or Bricks meta — including custom post types like
bricks_template that list_pages/list_posts never surface, since they are
not registered for the normal REST posts endpoints.
BuilderScanItem.title: BuilderScanItem

tools.name: create_post
tools.description: Create a WordPress post or page with Gutenberg content, optional category, Polylang language, and Rank Math SEO fields. Content is given as an ordered list of {type, text, level} blocks — 'heading' or 'paragraph' — which this tool renders into Gutenberg block markup. Defaults to a draft.

PostBlockInput.description:
One content block, already decided by the caller — no document parsing here.

type == "heading" renders <h{level}>; anything else renders a paragraph.

level.description: Heading level, used only when type is 'heading'
level.title: Level

PostBlockInput.title: PostBlockInput

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_type.description: 'post', 'page', or a custom post type's slug
post_type.title: Post Type

status.description: Initial status: draft, publish, pending, private, or future
status.title: Status

slug.description: Optional URL slug; WordPress derives one from the title if omitted
slug.title: Slug

blocks.description: Content as an ordered list of {type, text, level} blocks, rendered into Gutenberg block markup
blocks.title: Blocks

category.description: Optional category name (posts only); resolved to an existing term, never created
category.title: Category

date.description: Optional publish/schedule date as YYYY-MM-DD or full ISO 8601; required when status='future'
date.title: Date

lang.description: Optional Polylang language code, e.g. 'en', 'ro' — requires Polylang on the site
lang.title: Lang

meta_title.description: Optional Rank Math SEO title, set in the same call
meta_title.title: Meta Title

meta_description.description: Optional Rank Math SEO meta description, set in the same call
meta_description.title: Meta Description

focus_keyword.description: Optional Rank Math focus keyword, set in the same call
focus_keyword.title: Focus Keyword

return_schema.description: Outcome of create_post/update_post: the WordPress post/page that was written.
return_schema.title: PostResult

tools.name: update_post
tools.description: Update selected fields of an existing WordPress post or page: title, status, slug, content (as {type, text, level} blocks), excerpt, category, or date. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

PostBlockInput.description:
One content block, already decided by the caller — no document parsing here.

type == "heading" renders <h{level}>; anything else renders a paragraph.

level.description: Heading level, used only when type is 'heading'
level.title: Level

PostBlockInput.title: PostBlockInput

site_id.description: Site id from a previous list_sites call — never invent it
site_id.title: Site Id

post_id.description: Numeric id of the post or page to update
post_id.title: Post Id

post_type.description: 'post', 'page', or a custom post type's slug — must match the item being updated
post_type.title: Post Type

title.description: New title; omit to keep it
title.title: Title

status.description: New status: draft, publish, pending, private, or future
status.title: Status

slug.description: New URL slug; omit to keep it
slug.title: Slug

blocks.description: Replace the content with these ordered {type, text, level} blocks; omit to keep existing content
blocks.title: Blocks

excerpt.description: New excerpt; omit to keep it
excerpt.title: Excerpt

category.description: New category name (posts only); resolved to an existing term, never created
category.title: Category

date.description: New publish/schedule date as YYYY-MM-DD or full ISO 8601
date.title: Date

return_schema.description: Outcome of create_post/update_post: the WordPress post/page that was written.
return_schema.title: PostResult
